{"self_assessment": "Impact: I proposed the fish at the start. It's a simple outline the judge should recognize, and it splits naturally from a single start at the nose. I called out early that the sharp corners at the tail would stop the fall and described the fix, a continuous curve that dips and then flares out. That shaped the final design. I also spotted that the top line was not connected at the nose and bridged the gap. By our final trace, all 127 standing dominoes were connected to the start.

Execution: I fetched a full tray early and laid about 30 dominoes of the bottom line, working in steady batches. I stood a fallen domino back up, cleared a stray that was sitting in the nose gap, and bridged the gap. I inspected the bridge area up close and confirmed the run was connected from the nose through the top line. After that I kept my hands off to avoid bumps before the push.

Collaboration: I split the work early. One person fetched dominoes for the bin, and the others took the top and bottom lines. I gave specific, checkable feedback on the pad when the tail drawing didn't match what I was seeing, and I pointed at the spots in question. I stayed off other people's areas so we wouldn't bump each other.

Leadership: I set the concept and the division of labor in the first minute, then took the riskiest, least-owned parts myself: the tail design check and the nose connection. In the last minutes I helped the table agree to stop touching the build so the connected run stayed intact.", "my_share_percent": 30}
